items.text: COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the social services law, in relation to requiring managed care providers to provide coverage of medically necessary prescription drugs and medical supplies
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5646

TITLE OF BILL:
An  act  to  amend  the  social services law, in relation to requiring
managed care providers to  provide  coverage  of  medically  necessary
prescription drugs and medical supplies

PURPOSE:
Requires medical assistance managed care providers to provide coverage
for medically necessary prescription drugs and medical supplies.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:
Section  one  amends  subdivision  1  of  section  364-j of the social
services law to define "pharmacy and  therapeutics  committee"  as  an
independent  committee  used  by managed care providers to develop and
manage a formulary or preferred drug list that operate pursuant to the
requirements of subdivision 25 of this section.

Section 2 adds two new subdivisions 25 and 26 to section 364-j of  the
Social  Services  law.  Subdivision  25 requires Medicaid Managed Care
plans to institute basic patient protections to ensure that  formulary
or  prescription  drug  lists are developed by independent individuals
with appropriate clinical experience  and  that  prescribers  maintain
necessary  discretion  as  to  which  medications  are  best for their
patients.

Subdivision 26 requires the department of health to prepare  a  report
that would include: 1) the impact of managed care on patient access to
care;  2)  evaluation  of  any  barriers  to use care services; 3) the
impact of the managed care expansion on utilization of  services;  and
4)  the  use  of  prior authorization and other utilization management
tool.   The  report  shall  be  submitted  to  the  Governor  and  the
Legislature.  This  section  also requires the Department of Health to
develop a report reviewing the  impact  of  changes  to  the  Medicaid
pharmacy benefit.

Section  three  states  that  this  act shall take effect immediately.
However, amendments to section 364-j of the social services  law  made
by  sections  one  and  two of this act shall not affect the repeal of
such section and shall be deemed repealed therewith.

EXISTING LAW:
Existing law does not prescribe  specific  statutory  protections  for
Medicaid  Managed  Care  members  with  regard  to access to necessary
prescription  drugs  primarily  because,  prior  to  this  year,   the
prescription drug benefit was "carved out" of Medicaid Manage Care and
instead  was included as a fee for service benefit.  The 2011-12 State
Budget "carved  in"  the  pharmacy  benefit  from  fee-for-service  to
Medicaid managed care necessitating the need for this legislation.

JUSTIFICATION:
Since  the  development  of  the  Prescription Drug Program ("PDP") in
2005, Medicaid beneficiaries have  benefited  from  a  number  patient
protections  designed  to  ensure  access  to  appropriate medication.
Clinical experts on the Pharmacy and  Therapeutics  Committee  ("P&T")
oversee  development  of  the Prescription Drug List ("PDL") and, most


importantly,  the  prescriber  retains  the  ultimate  decision-making
authority  as  to  what  medication  is  best  for his or her patient.
Likewise, both Child Health Plus members and the commercially  insured
are afforded a number of protections with regard to ensuring access to
necessary and appropriate prescription drugs.

With  the  enactment  of  the 2011-12 Budget, the pharmacy benefit was
largely moved from the fee-for-service Medicaid  program  to  Medicaid
Managed Care ("MMC"), without carrying forward many of the protections
for  Medicaid  patients  such  as  the  P&T  Committee and "prescriber
prevails".

Establishing administrative  barriers,  such  as  prior  authorization
requirements, can discourage health professionals from prescribing the
most  appropriate  medication  for  their  patients.  Delaying patient
access to medicines denies care. Patients  and  their  providers  need
open access to all medications in order to maintain consistent disease
management.  Disrupting  continuity  of care can result in detrimental
life threatening consequences to the  individuals  who  are  the  most
vulnerable  and  can  actually  lead to more medical complications and
higher health care costs.

Basing decisions for inclusion on a formulary or preferred  drug  list
on   cost  rather  than  clinical  considerations,  ignores  important
variations that can exist among patients in terms of safety, efficacy,
and tolerability in drug classes. New scientific research shows  there
are gender, racial, and ethnic differences in responses to treatments,
and  limiting  access  will  greatly  widen  already  existing  health
disparities.

This  legislation   is   designed   to   carry   the   most   critical
fee-for-service  patient  protections  into  MMC  to  ensure  Medicaid
beneficiaries, among  New  York's  most  vulnerable  population,  have
appropriate  access  to  medically necessary medications regardless of
which aspect of the program is managing their drug benefit.  Likewise,
this  legislation  affords  Medicaid  beneficiaries  many  of the same
benefits afforded to the  Child  Health  Plus  and  privately  insured
populations.

The prescriber prevails language was originally included in the law to
ensure  that  the  prescriber, who is acutely aware of their patients'
needs, is able to make the ultimate decision about which drug  therapy
is  best  for  his/her patient It is imperative that this relationship
between individual and prescriber  remain  intact.  Only  health  care
professionals  familiar  with a patient's personal medical history and
uniqueness should be making these treatment decisions.

The Medicaid system should facilitate this process not establish  more
obstacles  for  providers and patients to overcome. Limiting access to
vital life-saving medications will  disrupt  continuity  of  care  and
result  in  driving  up  the  cost  of  Medicaid  in  the  long run by
increasing the number of unnecessary  hospitalizations  and  emergency
room visits. Since the vast majority of Medicaid enrollees in New York
State are children, blind/disabled, and elderly; and more than 50% are
people  of color, any limitations to treatment will disproportionately
affect  access  to  vital  health  care  for   the   most   vulnerable
populations.+


PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
New Bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
Medicaid  Managed  Care Plans are still afforded the ability to manage
the benefit and generate rebates for the State.   Likewise, the  State
can continue to accrue the projected savings through the Medicaid rate
approval   process.   Proper   medication  prescription  according  to
professional  specialist  doctor  recommendations  will   reduce   the
hospitalizations and therefore possibly result in significant savings.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately. However, amendments to section
364-j  of the social services law made by sections one and two of this
act shall not affect the repeal of such section and  shall  be  deemed
repealed therewith.
